Incoming shortwave radiation on the pixel plane

Source: R/metric-radiation.R
ef_rs_in.Rd

Computes the instantaneous incoming (downwelling) shortwave radiation \(R_{s\downarrow}\) on the plane of each pixel (horizontal or tilted) at the overpass time, separating the direct beam, the diffuse sky radiation and the radiation reflected by the surrounding ground. The total element is the rs_in argument of ef_net_radiation().

ef_rs_in() is the dispatcher of the family: it checks method (no default), forwards the other arguments to the method function, builds the diagnostic flags and records the provenance. The methods are:

  • ef_rs_in_modelled() (method = "modelled"): clear-sky radiation from the extraterrestrial irradiance and the partitioned transmissivity of ef_tau_sw_allen();

  • ef_rs_in_measured() (method = "measured"): measured (or regionalised) global radiation on the horizontal, split with a given diffuse fraction.

Both methods project the horizontal components onto the pixel plane in the same way.

Usage

ef_rs_in(..., method)

ef_rs_in_modelled(
  cos_zenith,
  cos_incidence,
  inv_distance,
  tau_beam,
  tau_diffuse,
  slope,
  ground_albedo = NULL
)

ef_rs_in_measured(
  rs_horizontal,
  diffuse_fraction,
  cos_zenith,
  cos_incidence,
  slope,
  ground_albedo = NULL
)

Arguments

...

Arguments passed to the method selected by method.

method

Character, no default. "modelled" or "measured".

cos_zenith

Numeric. Cosine of the solar zenith angle on the horizontal \(\cos\theta_h\) [-], in (0, 1] (ef_solar_geometry()$cos_zenith).

cos_incidence

Numeric. Cosine of the solar incidence angle on the pixel plane \(\cos\theta_{rel}\) [-], in [-1, 1] (ef_solar_geometry()$cos_incidence, computed with the same slope).

inv_distance

Numeric. Inverse relative Earth-Sun distance \(d_r\) [-], > 0 (ef_solar_geometry()$inv_distance).

tau_beam, tau_diffuse

Numeric. Direct-beam and diffuse clear-sky transmissivities on the horizontal [-] (ef_tau_sw_allen()$beam and $diffuse), each in [0, 1), with a sum in (0, 1).

slope

Numeric, no default. Slope of the pixel plane [rad], in [0, pi/2]; the same slope used to compute cos_incidence (0 for a horizontal plane).

ground_albedo

Numeric or NULL. Albedo of the ground seen by the tilted plane \(\rho_g\) [-], in [0, 1] (for example the albedo of the pixel itself or a neighbourhood mean, decision RC-09). Required when any slope > 0; may be NULL on flat terrain, where the reflected term is zero.

rs_horizontal

Numeric. Measured or regionalised global shortwave radiation on the horizontal at the overpass time [W m-2], >= 0.

diffuse_fraction

Numeric, no default. Diffuse fraction of rs_horizontal \(k_d\) [-], in [0, 1]. How to obtain it (clear-sky model, decomposition model or hybrid) is an open decision (RC-10).

Value

A plain list (no class) of numeric vectors with the common length and dim of the inputs:

  • total: \(R_{s\downarrow}\) on the pixel plane [W m-2];

  • beam, diffuse, reflected: its direct-beam, diffuse-sky and ground-reflected components [W m-2];

  • diffuse_fraction (ef_rs_in_modelled() only): diffuse fraction of the clear-sky radiation on the horizontal, \(\tau_d / (\tau_b + \tau_d)\) [-].

ef_rs_in() returns a list of class earthflux_incoming_shortwave with the same elements for both methods (type-stable): total, beam, diffuse and reflected (identical to those of the method function), diffuse_fraction (NULL for "measured", where it is an input), method, flags (one record per code that holds somewhere: EF_INPUT_NA and EF_RAD_SELF_SHADED; see Details) and provenance (method, method function, verification status, inputs used, flag codes evaluated in flags_evaluated, EarthFlux version).

Details

Components on the horizontal:

  • ef_rs_in_modelled(): \(R_{a,h} = G_{sc} d_r \cos\theta_h\), \(R_{b,h} = \tau_b R_{a,h}\) and \(R_{d,h} = \tau_d R_{a,h}\), with \(G_{sc}\) the solar constant of the package (1366.67 W m-2, FAO-56 Eq. 21; the SEBAL Idaho manual rounds it to 1367 W m-2, RC-06);

  • ef_rs_in_measured(): \(R_{b,h} = (1 - k_d) R_{s,meas}\) and \(R_{d,h} = k_d R_{s,meas}\).

Projection onto the plane of slope \(s\) (isotropic diffuse sky and isotropic ground reflection, unobstructed horizon): $$R_{b,s} = R_{b,h} \frac{\max(\cos\theta_{rel}, 0)}{\cos\theta_h}, \quad R_{d,s} = R_{d,h} \frac{1 + \cos s}{2}, \quad R_{r,s} = \rho_g (R_{b,h} + R_{d,h}) \frac{1 - \cos s}{2}$$ and \(R_{s\downarrow} = R_{b,s} + R_{d,s} + R_{r,s}\). In the modelled path \(R_{b,s} = \tau_b G_{sc} d_r \max(\cos\theta_{rel}, 0)\). On flat terrain (\(s = 0\), \(\cos\theta_{rel} = \cos\theta_h\)) the modelled radiation reduces to \(G_{sc} d_r \cos\theta_h \tau_{sw}\).

A plane facing away from the sun (\(\cos\theta_{rel} \le 0\)) receives no direct beam: \(\max(\cos\theta_{rel}, 0)\) is the physical definition of the beam irradiance on that plane, not a correction, and is reported by ef_rs_in() with the flag EF_RAD_SELF_SHADED. The resulting radiation is never truncated.

Diagnostics (ef_rs_in() only; the method functions return values without flags). EF_INPUT_NA: a required input is missing at the position; EF_RAD_SELF_SHADED: the sun is above the horizon but the pixel plane faces away from it. A record is present only for a code that holds somewhere; the codes evaluated are in provenance$flags_evaluated.

Unlike a common simplified form, \(G_{sc} d_r \cos\theta_{rel} \tau_{sw}\), the diffuse component is not projected as if it were direct beam; on slopes the two forms differ by tens to hundreds of W m-2.

Assumptions: clear sky (modelled path); no cast shadows and no reduction of the sky view by the surrounding relief; isotropic diffuse sky and ground reflection; instantaneous values at the overpass time. Measured radiation is usually a 10-60 min mean and must be interpolated to the overpass time upstream.

Arguments must be numeric and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, matrix or array arguments must share their dim. Values outside the domains above (including cos_zenith <= 0, sun below the horizon) or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). ground_albedo = NULL with a positive slope raises earthflux_missing_input. A missing or unknown method raises earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method; an argument required by the chosen method but not supplied to the dispatcher raises earthflux_missing_input, and one the method does not accept raises earthflux_input_error. Missing values propagate arithmetically to the outputs that depend on them, and always to total.

Verification status

The modelled form on flat terrain is VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): \(G_{sc} \cos\theta\, d_r\, \tau_{sw}\), Waters et al. (2002), p. 19, Eq. 12 (the manual rounds \(G_{sc}\) to 1367 W m-2; the package uses the FAO-56 value 1366.67 W m-2, a relative difference of 2.4e-4, decision RC-06).

On slopes the form is CANDIDATA and differs from the mountain model of the manual (appendix 12, pp. 93-95), which applies Eq. 12 with the cosine of the incidence angle on the slope divided by the cosine of the slope ("horizontal equivalent") and one total transmissivity, without a beam / diffuse partition. EarthFlux projects the beam and diffuse components separately onto the plane (isotropic projection of solar engineering texts, Duffie and Beckman; isotropic model attributed to Liu and Jordan; neither verified); whether Allen, Trezza and Tasumi (2006) prescribe an anisotropic diffuse term is TODO (decision RC-09). In the measured path, the source of the diffuse fraction is TODO (decision RC-10).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

See also

Other radiation functions: ef_atm_emissivity(), ef_net_radiation(), ef_rl_in(), ef_rl_out(), ef_solar_geometry(), ef_tau_sw()

Examples

deg <- pi / 180
# Clear-sky radiation on a horizontal pixel and on a 20 degree
# north-facing slope (southern hemisphere)
geo <- ef_solar_geometry(doy = 15, utc_hour = 15.5, lat = -35 * deg,
                         lon = -71 * deg, slope = c(0, 20) * deg,
                         aspect = 0)
tau <- ef_tau_sw_allen(geo$cos_zenith, ef_air_pressure(500),
                       vapour_pressure = 1.2, turbidity = 1)
rs <- ef_rs_in(
  cos_zenith = geo$cos_zenith, cos_incidence = geo$cos_incidence,
  inv_distance = geo$inv_distance, tau_beam = tau$beam,
  tau_diffuse = tau$diffuse, slope = c(0, 20) * deg,
  ground_albedo = 0.2, method = "modelled"
)
rs$total
#> [1] 1001.852 1016.459
rs$provenance$flags_evaluated
#> [1] "EF_INPUT_NA"        "EF_RAD_SELF_SHADED"

# Measured global radiation on the horizontal, projected to the slopes
ef_rs_in_measured(
  rs_horizontal = 950, diffuse_fraction = 0.15,
  cos_zenith = geo$cos_zenith, cos_incidence = geo$cos_incidence,
  slope = c(0, 20) * deg, ground_albedo = 0.2
)$total
#> [1] 950.0000 963.7109
